from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        accel_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1, color="#FFFF00")

        accel_group = VGroup(accel_arrow, accel_label).arrange(DOWN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(cheetah_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF8C00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Placing velocity arrow according to critic
        self.place_in_area(velocity_arrow, 'B4', 'B6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(GrowArrow(velocity_arrow), Write(velocity_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Using fix for acceleration label
        self.place_at_grid(accel_label, 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        accel_arrow.next_to(cheetah, DOWN)
        self.play(GrowArrow(accel_arrow), Write(accel_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Indicate(velocity_arrow), Indicate(accel_arrow))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(cheetah.animate.shift(RIGHT*1), velocity_arrow.animate.shift(RIGHT*1), accel_arrow.animate.shift(RIGHT*1))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Concavity relates to the second derivative.",
            "Positive values mean concave up.",
            "Negative values mean concave down."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Interpretation: Concavity", lecture_lines)
        
        # Axes and Function
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-8, 8], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        func = lambda x: x**3
        graph = axes.plot(func, color=WHITE)
        
        # Fix 1: Adjust axes size and position
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.5)
        graph.set_color(WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(axes), Create(graph))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        tangent = Line(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color="#00FFFF").scale(0.3)
        t = ValueTracker(1.0)
        
        # Tangent line logic
        tangent.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(t.get_value(), func(t.get_value()))))
        self.add(tangent)
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(1.5))
        
        # Fix 3: Grouping for derivative label
        f_double_prime = Tex(r"f''(x) > 0", color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(f_double_prime, "E6", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(f_double_prime))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        t.set_value(-1.0)
        
        # Fix 2: Adjust label position
        label = Tex(r"f''(x) < 0", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A2", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(-1.5), FadeIn(label))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Higher Order Derivatives: The Dynamics of Motion

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Running Cheetah
sections.content: Introduce the concept of rate of change using a cheetah: Position (m), Velocity (m/s), and Acceleration (m/s²). Explain that just as velocity is the derivative of position, acceleration is the derivative of velocity—forming a 'chain of rates'.
sections.example: Visualizing a cheetah accelerating: Plotting position vs. time (a curve), velocity vs. time (the slope of the curve), and acceleration (the slope of the velocity).

sections.title: Defining Higher Order Derivatives
sections.content: Formalize the notation: f'(x) is the 1st derivative, f''(x) is the 2nd derivative, and fⁿ⁾(x) represents the n-th derivative. Emphasize that each step measures the 'rate of change of the previous rate'.
sections.example: Mathematical notation evolution: f(x) → f'(x) → f''(x) → f'''(x) → f⁽⁴⁾(x), showing how the power rule (d/dx xⁿ) cascades.

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation: Concavity
sections.content: Connect the 2nd derivative to the physical shape of the graph. f''(x) > 0 indicates 'Concave Up' (like a cup holding water), while f''(x) < 0 indicates 'Concave Down' (like an umbrella shedding rain).
sections.example: An animated graph of f(x) = x³ transitioning from concave down to concave up at the inflection point x=0, with dynamic tangent lines demonstrating the change.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Calculation Practice
sections.content: Walk through a polynomial differentiation sequence. Use a simple cubic function to demonstrate that the higher the derivative, the simpler the function becomes until it reaches zero.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Application
sections.content: Recap: 1st derivative = Velocity/Slope; 2nd derivative = Acceleration/Concavity. Briefly mention that higher order derivatives are essential in engineering for 'Jerk' (the 3rd derivative) in elevator design to ensure passenger comfort.
sections.example: An animation of an elevator starting smoothly vs. abruptly, controlled by the 3rd derivative of position (Jerk).
